definition: A storage method that uses low-cost off-peak power to run an air compressor, forcing air into a storage vessel; the compressed air can later be released to run a turbine for electricity, used directly as pneumatic power, or used for heating/cooling because it cools rapidly as it expands.
core_idea: Compressed air storage banks cheap night/weekend power as pressurized air, which can later be converted back to electricity via a turbine, used directly to power pneumatic tools, or exploited for an HVAC application because expanding compressed gas cools rapidly.
key_points: The compressor runs during low-price periods, such as nights or weekends, to fill the storage vessel.
Sufficiently high air pressure can drive a turbine to regenerate electricity when needed.
Compressed air can also be used directly, for example to run pneumatic tools common in industrial jobs.
Because compressed gas cools rapidly as it expands, the author notes it could support a heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) use case.
trading_implications: Compressed air storage has multiple potential use paths (electricity regeneration, direct pneumatic use, HVAC), which broadens how a facility might be valued beyond pure electricity price arbitrage.
